Okay, let's see. I need to compute 17 multiplied by 19. Hmm, how do I approach this? Well, maybe I can break it down into easier parts. Let me think. I remember that multiplying numbers close to 20 might be easier if I use some tricks.

Wait, 17 times 20 would be 340, right? Because 17 times 2 is 34, so times 10 is 340. But since 19 is one less than 20, maybe I can subtract 17 from 340? Let me check that. So 17 × 19 is the same as 17 × (20 - 1), which is 17×20 - 17×1. That would be 340 - 17. What's 340 minus 17? Let me calculate that. 340 minus 10 is 330, then minus 7 more is 323. Oh, so the result is 323. Let me verify that another way to make sure I didn't make a mistake.

Alternatively, I can use the standard multiplication method. Let's do 17 × 19. First, multiply 17 by 9. 17×9 is 153. Then multiply 17 by 10, which is 170. Wait, no, actually, when you do vertical multiplication, it's 17 × 19. So 19 is 9 in the ones place and 1 in the tens place. So 17 × 9 = 153, and then 17 × 1 (which is actually 10) = 170. Then add them together: 153 + 170. Let's add those. 153 + 170. 150 + 170 is 320, and then +3 is 323. Yep, same result. So that confirms it. Both methods give me 323. I think that's correct. Let me just check with another method. Maybe using the formula (a + b)(a - b) = a² - b². Wait, but 17 and 19 are both around 18. Let me see. If I take 18 as the middle number, then 17 is 18 -1 and 19 is 18 +1. So (18 -1)(18 +1) = 18² -1². 18 squared is 324, minus 1 is 323. Oh, that's a neat way to see it. So that also gives 323. All three methods lead to the same answer. I'm confident that 17 × 19 equals 323.
